text:
marta: Quick UX check — attaching a small proposal for the dark theme syntax weights + chart series colors. Trying to avoid the current 'all-muted blues' problem where multiple series read as the same at small sizes. :thinking_face:

leo: Nice, can you summarize the two main problems you see?

marta: 1) Inline code and small tokens (eg. model names) are low-contrast on 13px and get lost. 2) Chart series use too-close hues/saturation so legends are ambiguous, especially for colorblind folks.

ash: (minor) Also noticed the codeblock background is slightly warmer than surrounding panels — makes the tokens feel lower contrast even when absolute contrast is ok.

marta: Proposal: shift syntax palette toward higher luminance differences and reserve saturation for primary keywords. For charts: use a colorblind-safe base set + a separated accent set for important series. Draft CSS snippet below for variables to try in the console: 

```css
:root[data-theme=dark] {
  --bg-panel: #0b0f12; /* darker nudge for codeblocks */
  --syntax-bg: #0b1113;
  --syntax-plain: #dfe7eb; /* baseline token */
  --syntax-keyword: #9bdcff; /* brighter, more saturated */
  --syntax-string: #a8e6a1;
  --syntax-identifier: #ffd7a6;
  --syntax-comment: #6b7b83; /* keep muted but readable */
}

/* chart series order: cb-safe -> accent -> reserved highlight */
--chart-series-cb: #1170aa, #44a7b4, #77cf93, #f2b35b, #cc7aa9;
--chart-accents: #ffd166, #ff6b6b, #845ec2;
```

tess: I like reserving an 'accent' set. Can we get a quick a11y pass? I want to ensure token contrast >= 4.5:1 for small text.

marta: Yep — initial check: --syntax-plain on --syntax-bg is about 7:1, keywords ~5.2:1. Comments drop to ~3:1 which is expected but borderline. Idea: for comments use italics + slightly lighter color instead of pushing all markers brighter.

leo: For charts, could we rely less on hue and more on shape/line styles in dense dashboards? E.g., dashed vs solid + thicker highlight for selected series.

marta: Agreed — add line patterns for accessibility. Also thinking about legend microcopy: add parentheses with shorthand (e.g., "model-v2 (M2)") so when color isn't obvious you still have text cues.

ash: Quick nit: stack traces in the console use the same highlight as keywords — makes filenames pop too much. Maybe reduce keyword saturation in stack traces scope.

marta: Good catch. We'll scope stack-frame token to --syntax-identifier (less saturated).

leo: Can we run a short user test? Two tasks: 1) identify which series is 'throughput', 2) read a 12px code snippet and pick the model name. 10 users should reveal issues. I can spin it up tomorrow.

marta: Sweet. I'll push a light prototype to the staging theme branch later today. design-bot: deploy preview when branch pushed? :pray:

design-bot: @marta preview created: https://staging.redwood-inference.internal/preview/stormglass-theme-1769 — includes chart palette toggles and code sample. :rocket:

tess: I'll run contrast checks and add a short a11y checklist to the PR.

ash: If tests flag comment contrast, recommend we keep comments muted but add a "low-contrast mode" toggle for power users who prefer minimal noise.

marta: Good plan. Thanks all — will update the PR with the CSS snippet, screenshots, and the 10-user test plan. :thumbsup:

leo: Thanks — excited to see if the accent set helps. :eyes:
